name: Whistler
tagline: North America's largest ski resort, reached by one of the continent's most scenic drives, with a genuine mountain village at its base.
highlight: Riding the Peak 2 Peak Gondola between Whistler and Blackcomb, the valley floor over 400 metres below the world's longest unsupported cable span.
shortDescription: North America's largest ski resort, reached via the scenic Sea to Sky Highway, with genuine year-round mountain adventure beyond winter sports.
metaDescription: A Whistler travel guide: the Peak 2 Peak Gondola, Whistler Blackcomb, Lost Lake, the Sea to Sky Highway, food and how to plan a visit.
nearestAirport: Vancouver International Airport (YVR), about 2.5 hours by road
knownFor: Whistler Blackcomb skiing, the Peak 2 Peak Gondola, the Sea to Sky Highway
budget: C$200–450 per day, mid-range to upscale (higher in ski season)

image.alt: Whistler Village beneath its surrounding mountains

intro: Whistler is genuinely North America's largest ski resort, twin mountains rising directly above a purpose-built alpine village about two hours north of Vancouver.
Getting there is genuinely part of the appeal — the Sea to Sky Highway ranks among the continent's most scenic drives, hugging Howe Sound before climbing into the Coast Mountains.
While winter sports genuinely built its reputation, Whistler has become just as much a summer destination, with mountain biking, hiking and lake swimming filling the resort's other half of the year.

whyVisit.intro: Whistler's case rests genuinely on world-class mountain terrain paired with a proper, walkable village at its base.

points.title: It's genuinely North America's largest ski resort
points.text: Two connected mountains, Whistler and Blackcomb, offering an enormous amount of terrain.

points.title: The Peak 2 Peak Gondola is genuinely an engineering feat
points.text: The world's longest unsupported cable span, linking the two mountains directly.

points.title: The Sea to Sky Highway is genuinely one of the best drives in North America
points.text: A dramatic coastal and mountain route between Vancouver and Whistler.

points.title: It's genuinely a real year-round destination
points.text: World-class mountain biking and hiking take over once the snow melts.

points.title: The village itself is genuinely well designed
points.text: A car-free, walkable base area built specifically around ski-in, ski-out convenience.

attractionsIntro: Whistler's essential sights are genuinely spread across its village, the mountains above it, and the drive to reach it.

attractions.name: Whistler Village

image.alt: Whistler Village at the base of the mountains

attractions.text: Genuinely a purpose-built, car-free alpine village, its cobbled squares lined with shops, restaurants and bars.
attractions.tip: Genuinely explore both Whistler Village and the smaller, quieter Village North just beyond it.

attractions.name: The Peak 2 Peak Gondola

image.file: File:Whistler end of the Peak to Peak gondola (7958946150).jpg
image.alt: The Peak 2 Peak Gondola connecting Whistler and Blackcomb

attractions.text: Genuinely the world's longest unsupported cable span, linking Whistler and Blackcomb mountains 436 metres above the valley.
attractions.tip: Genuinely ride it even if you're not skiing — it runs for sightseers too, with glass-bottomed cabins on some cars.

attractions.name: Whistler Blackcomb's slopes

image.alt: The ski slopes at Whistler Blackcomb

attractions.text: Genuinely North America's largest ski resort by terrain, with runs for every level across two connected mountains.
attractions.tip: Genuinely book lift tickets and rentals online ahead in peak ski season.

attractions.name: Lost Lake
attractions.text: Genuinely a peaceful escape from the village, a forested lake with swimming, paddling and a network of trails.
attractions.tip: Genuinely an easy walk or bike ride from Whistler Village itself.

attractions.name: The Sea to Sky Gondola

image.alt: The Sea to Sky Gondola near Squamish

attractions.text: Genuinely worth the stop on the drive up, a gondola near Squamish climbing to sweeping views over Howe Sound.
attractions.tip: Genuinely combine with a walk across the suspension bridge at the summit.

attractions.name: The Stawamus Chief viewpoint

image.file: File:Stawamus Chief from Chief Overlook Panorama Trail Sea to Sky Gondola Squamish dllu.jpg
image.alt: The Stawamus Chief seen from the Sea to Sky Gondola

attractions.text: Genuinely a dramatic granite monolith near Squamish, one of the largest in the world, visible from the Sea to Sky Gondola.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a popular rock-climbing destination for those with the skill and gear.

attractions.name: Whistler's mountain backdrop
attractions.text: Genuinely striking in any season, jagged Coast Mountain peaks rising directly above the village.
attractions.tip: Genuinely the view changes dramatically between summer green and winter snow — worth a visit in both.

thingsToDoIntro: Whistler genuinely offers something in every season, not just the winter sports it's best known for.

thingsToDo.title: Ride the Peak 2 Peak Gondola between the mountains
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential Whistler experience, gliding between two mountains high above the valley floor.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely go on a clear day for the best views — cloud cover can obscure the panorama entirely.

thingsToDo.title: Ski or snowboard Whistler Blackcomb

image.file: File:Big snowdrifts at the top of Whistler Mtn. (16153313445).jpg

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely world-class winter sports experience, with terrain for complete beginners through to experts.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely book lessons ahead if you're new — Whistler's ski schools are excellent but do fill up.

thingsToDo.title: Hike or bike around Lost Lake

image.file: File:View on Lost Lake, Whistler B.C.jpg
image.alt: Hiking around Lost Lake near Whistler

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely relaxed way to spend a summer afternoon, swimming, paddling or cycling the surrounding trails.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a nice alternative when the village itself feels too busy.

thingsToDo.title: Ride the Sea to Sky Gondola near Squamish

image.alt: The view from the Sea to Sky Gondola

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely worthwhile detour on the drive up, sweeping views over Howe Sound from a suspension bridge viewpoint.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely budget an hour or two here if travelling by car between Vancouver and Whistler.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the Squamish Lil'wat Cultural Centre
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely worthwhile stop in Whistler Village itself, showcasing the art and history of the region's First Nations.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely check for guided tours, which add real depth to the exhibits.

thingsToDo.title: Relax at an outdoor spa after a day on the mountain
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely popular way to unwind, alternating between hot pools, saunas and cold plunges in a forest setting.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely book ahead — Whistler's outdoor spas are popular and slots do fill up.

accommodation.intro: Whistler genuinely offers everything from hostels to ski-in, ski-out luxury, with prices climbing steeply in peak ski season.

areas.name: Whistler Village
areas.bestFor: Being genuinely ski-in, ski-out and within walking distance of everything

areas.name: Creekside or Upper Village
areas.bestFor: A genuinely quieter, slightly better value stay

gettingThere.intro: Whistler is genuinely reached by road from Vancouver, with no airport of its own.

options.mode: Drive the Sea to Sky Highway from Vancouver
options.text: Genuinely the standard route, taking about 2.5 hours.
options.detail: One of the most scenic drives in North America, hugging Howe Sound before climbing into the mountains.

options.mode: Shuttle bus from Vancouver or the airport
options.text: Genuinely convenient if you'd rather not drive.
options.detail: Several operators run frequent direct services, especially in ski season.

options.text: Genuinely the most flexible option for stopping along the way.
options.detail: Allows stops at the Sea to Sky Gondola and other viewpoints en route.

gettingAround.intro: Whistler Village is genuinely car-free and entirely walkable, with lifts and shuttles covering the mountains.

options.text: Genuinely the only way to move through the village itself.
options.detail: Cars are largely restricted from the pedestrian core.

options.text: Genuinely the way up the mountains, whether skiing or sightseeing.
options.detail: A single pass typically covers both Whistler and Blackcomb.

options.text: Genuinely useful for reaching Creekside or other outlying areas.
options.detail: A free or low-cost shuttle connects the village's different zones.

bestTime.headline: December to March for skiing, June to September for hiking and biking
bestTime.summary: Whistler is genuinely a true year-round resort, with two distinct high seasons depending on what you're after.

seasons.text: Genuinely prime ski season, with the most reliable snow and the resort at its liveliest.
Genuinely excellent for mountain biking, hiking and lake swimming, with warm, sunny weather.
Genuinely a quieter shoulder season, still pleasant for hiking before the snow returns.
Genuinely the quietest, muddiest months, with limited activities as the resort transitions between seasons.

bestTime.avoid: Genuinely late spring (April–May) and late autumn (November), when neither skiing nor summer activities are fully available.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Whistler visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book genuinely lift tickets, rentals and lessons online ahead for peak ski season.
Pack genuinely for both warm days and cold mornings, even in summer.
Stop genuinely at the Sea to Sky Gondola on the drive up if you have the time.
Book genuinely accommodation months ahead for peak ski season or summer weekends.
Bring genuinely a swimsuit for Lost Lake, even on a winter visit — some spas keep pools open year-round.
Consider genuinely a shuttle from Vancouver if you'd rather not drive the Sea to Sky Highway.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Whistler?
faq.a: Two to three days genuinely covers the mountains and village comfortably, longer if skiing is the main focus.

faq.q: How do you get from Vancouver to Whistler?
faq.a: Genuinely by car or shuttle bus along the Sea to Sky Highway, taking about 2.5 hours.

faq.q: Is Whistler only good for skiing?
faq.a: No, genuinely not — summer brings excellent mountain biking, hiking and lake activities, making it a true year-round destination.
Genuinely one of Canada's pricier destinations, especially in peak ski season, though summer offers noticeably better value.

faq.q: Do you need to be an expert skier to enjoy Whistler?
faq.a: No, genuinely not — the resort has extensive terrain and lessons for complete beginners through to experts.

faq.q: Can you visit Whistler without skiing?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely easily — the Peak 2 Peak Gondola, Lost Lake and the village itself are all worthwhile without touching a ski.
